items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: Abe Ed Lyman sent for you.

ctx.x: Bill Johnson to play in my place, you know. Take my place. But he gets back to New York, all right, he sends me a telegram that he wants me to come on. "Make up your mind." "No, I ain't going, Joe." So I leaves California -- Los Angeles, and go back to Oakland. Joe sent me a ticket there in Oakland to come to New York. And I told him, "Yeah, I'm coming." And I get the ticket, and I had a Studebaker. I sold my Studebaker to the man where I (And this is true from here to heaven, in the garage.) used to park the…

that's Orrie. Said, "Man, I just come here for you." I said, "Come here for me?" He said, "What you doing down here?" I said, "I'm fixing to go and get this ticket. I'm going to New York." "Going to New York?" He said, "Man, Abe Ed Lyman sent for you." "We're going to wait for him." And at that time, Abe Lyman had a place on Spring, near 5th.
